quizzes.title: Masterpiece Moments
quizzes.description: The world's most famous paintings and the artists who made them.

questions.q: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.note: It is thought to portray Lisa Gherardini, a woman from Florence.

questions.q: Which artist painted "The Starry Night"?
questions.note: He painted it in 1889 while staying at an asylum in Saint-Rémy.

questions.q: Michelangelo painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
questions.note: He worked on the ceiling from 1508 to 1512.

questions.q: Which artist painted "The Scream"?
questions.note: The Norwegian artist made several versions, the first in 1893.

questions.q: Which Spanish artist co-founded Cubism with Georges Braque?
questions.note: Accept Pablo Picasso.

questions.q: Salvador Dalí's melting clocks appear in which painting?
questions.note: Painted in 1931, it hangs at MoMA in New York.

questions.q: The Mona Lisa is displayed in the British Museum in London.
questions.note: It hangs in the Louvre in Paris, behind protective glass.

questions.q: Which Dutch artist painted "Girl with a Pearl Earring"?
questions.note: Painted around 1665, it hangs in the Mauritshuis in The Hague.

questions.q: Which French Impressionist painted a famous series of water lilies in his garden?
questions.note: Accept Claude Monet; the garden was at his home in Giverny.

questions.q: Which Renaissance artist painted "The Birth of Venus"?
questions.note: It hangs in the Uffizi Gallery in Florence.

quizzes.title: Wonders of Architecture
quizzes.description: Famous buildings, landmarks and the minds that designed them.

questions.q: Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal?
questions.note: He built it as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.q: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair in Paris.
questions.note: It was the world's tallest man-made structure until 1930.

questions.q: Which architect designed the Sagrada Família in Barcelona?
questions.note: Construction began in 1882 and is still continuing.

questions.q: Who designed the Sydney Opera House?
questions.note: The Danish architect's building opened in 1973.

questions.q: Which temple complex in Cambodia is the largest religious monument in the world?
questions.note: Built in the 12th century, it appears on Cambodia's national flag.

questions.q: Which famous house by Frank Lloyd Wright is built over a waterfall?
questions.note: It was built in rural Pennsylvania in the late 1930s.

questions.q: The Parthenon in Athens was dedicated to the god Zeus.
questions.note: It was dedicated to Athena, the patron goddess of Athens.

questions.q: Petra, the ancient city carved into rose-red rock, is in which country?
questions.note: It was the capital of the Nabataean kingdom.

questions.q: In which city does St Basil's Cathedral, with its colourful onion domes, stand?
questions.note: It stands on Red Square and was completed in 1561.

questions.q: Which Istanbul landmark has served as a church, a mosque and a museum?
questions.note: Completed in AD 537, it was turned back into a mosque in 2020.

quizzes.title: Dance & Traditions
quizzes.description: Dances, festivals and cultural traditions from around the globe.

questions.q: Which country is the tango most closely associated with?
questions.note: It emerged in Buenos Aires and Montevideo in the late 1800s.

questions.q: Flamenco is a traditional art form from Spain.
questions.note: It is linked above all with Andalusia and was listed by UNESCO in 2010.

questions.q: Kathakali, known for its elaborate face paint, comes from which Indian state?
questions.note: Performers can take hours to apply the green-faced make-up of the heroic characters.

questions.q: What is the Japanese art of paper folding called?
questions.note: The word comes from ori (folding) and kami (paper).

questions.q: Which dance do New Zealand's All Blacks perform before rugby matches?
questions.note: The haka is a traditional Māori ceremonial dance.

questions.q: Which composer wrote the music for the ballet "Swan Lake"?
questions.note: It premiered at Moscow's Bolshoi Theatre in 1877.

questions.q: The samba dance originated in Argentina.
questions.note: Samba comes from Brazil and is the heartbeat of Rio's Carnival.

questions.q: Which Japanese theatre form is known for stylised acting and bold make-up?
questions.note: Noh performers wear masks, and Bunraku uses large puppets.

questions.q: Which Irish dance show began as the interval act at Eurovision 1994?
questions.note: The contest was held in Dublin that year.

questions.q: The Hindu festival Diwali is widely known as the festival of what?
questions.note: Holi is the festival of colours; at Diwali, clay lamps called diyas are lit.

quizzes.title: Brushstrokes & Movements
quizzes.description: Deeper cuts on great artists, sculptors and art movements.

questions.q: Who painted "The Night Watch"?
questions.note: Completed in 1642, it is the star of Amsterdam's Rijksmuseum.

questions.q: André Breton wrote the first Surrealist Manifesto in 1924.
questions.note: Salvador Dalí and René Magritte became the movement's best-known painters.

questions.q: Who painted "The Garden of Earthly Delights"?
questions.note: The triptych hangs in the Prado Museum in Madrid.

questions.q: Which Japanese artist created the woodblock print "The Great Wave off Kanagawa"?
questions.note: Accept Katsushika Hokusai; the print dates from the early 1830s.

questions.q: Which Dutch painter is famous for grids of black lines and blocks of primary colour?
questions.note: Many of these works are simply titled Composition.

questions.q: Which Austrian painter created "The Kiss", decorated with gold leaf?
questions.note: Painted in 1907–1908, it hangs in the Belvedere in Vienna.

questions.q: Michelangelo's statue of David is cast in bronze.
questions.note: It was carved from a single block of marble between 1501 and 1504.

questions.q: Which sculptor created "The Thinker"?
questions.note: It was first conceived as part of his great bronze doors, The Gates of Hell.

questions.q: Which Mexican muralist was married to the painter Frida Kahlo?
questions.note: Accept Rivera; the couple first married in 1929.

questions.q: Kazimir Malevich's "Black Square" is a landmark of which art movement?
questions.note: Malevich first exhibited it in 1915 in Petrograd.
